findings: PointerList reader constructs its index spine from the stored binary word and traverses actual immutable pair fields; return restores the real caller and exact source.
Matrix reader retrieves the actual stored row pointer and then stored flag, with exact row+column+2 allocations and composed instruction count. Bounds are explicit.

Walk extension executes actual outgoing source-zero cost access and canonical rational addition, retains the preexisting ordered edge pair, prepends it to the stored edge list, and allocates the exact scratch/list/walk records.
Relocation slots and saved-stack preservation use instruction-level contracts; no arbitrary host adjacency or addition callback is supplied.
scope_limits: These are bounded storage/arithmetic foundations, not graph path-discovery correctness.

GraphWalkExtension.Walk is a stored edge-list/cost record; valid adjacency, endpoint continuity and numeric cost interpretation must be established by the real caller. The theorem correctly assumes none of these and claims only its exact representation transformation.
Matrix construction from the actual input graph, recursive relaxation scan, input-derived runtime and full theorem joins remain outside this three-source review.
No compiler was invoked by reviewer; production gates and full CI remain separate.
